children: Brazil's central bank said on Tuesday that trends in non-earmarked lending were consistent with a slowdown in economic growth, as tight monetary policy continued to restrain activity in the Latin America's largest economy.

In the minutes of last week's policy meeting, at which it cut the benchmark Selic rate by 25 basis points to 13.75%, policymakers highlighted a decline in longer-term non-earmarked credit lines, which tend to be more sensitive to monetary policy than costlier short-term and emergency borrowing.
